s1.syndrome_frame: Postoperative skin lesion with erythema and nodules over a mastectomy site
salient_findings: Pruritic erythema lesion with multiple nodules over the operation site of the right breast
Well-demarcated, warm, erythematous plaque over the right side of the anterior chest wall
Multiple emboli of carcinoma cells in dermal and subcutaneous lymphatic vessels
key_facts: History of right breast cancer, stage IIIa (cT2N2M0)
Underwent neoadjuvant chemotherapy followed by right modified radical mastectomy and postoperative radiotherapy
Noticed a pruritic erythema lesion with multiple nodules over the operation site after radiotherapy
Lesion did not respond to initial topical treatments
Presented to dermatology for evaluation of skin erythema over her right breast 1 year after initial cancer diagnosis
Erythematous plaque measured 15 × 12 cm
Multiple palpable small nodules scattered within the erythema
Immunohistochemistry negative for estrogen receptor (ER), progesterone receptor (PR), and human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)

shortlist.label: Inflammatory breast carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: History of breast cancer and presence of erythema and nodules over the mastectomy site

shortlist.label: Metastatic carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: History of breast cancer and presence of carcinoma cells in dermal and subcutaneous lymphatic vessels

shortlist.label: Angiosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of erythematous plaque and nodules, which are common features of angiosarcoma

shortlist.label: Stewart-Treves syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: History of mastectomy and presence of lymphangiosarcoma-like features

shortlist.label: Radiation-induced sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: History of radiotherapy and presence of a new skin lesion over the irradiated area

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of a pruritic erythema lesion with multiple nodules over the operation site, which did not respond to initial topical treatments, along with the histopathological finding of multiple emboli of carcinoma cells in dermal and subcutaneous lymphatic vessels, is consistent with inflammatory breast carcinoma, especially given her history of breast cancer.

rejected.label: Metastatic carcinoma
rejected.why: While possible, the specific presentation and histopathology suggest a more localized aggressive process rather than distant metastasis.

rejected.label: Angiosarcoma
rejected.why: The clinical presentation and histopathological findings do not specifically suggest a sarcoma of blood vessel origin.

rejected.label: Stewart-Treves syndrome
rejected.why: This condition refers to angiosarcoma arising in the context of chronic lymphedema, which is not indicated in this patient's history.

rejected.label: Radiation-induced sarcoma
rejected.why: The timeframe and the nature of the lesion do not align well with radiation-induced sarcoma, which typically occurs years after radiation exposure and would not typically present with carcinoma cells in lymphatic vessels.
